newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra sees double-digit FY97 EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra sees double-digit FY97 EPS growth.

text.p: ConAgra Inc said Thursday it expects double-digit earnings per share growth in fiscal 1997.

"For the full year, we continue to expect double-digit earnings per share growth and ConAgra's 17th consecutive year of record earnings, excluding the non-recurring charges in last year's fourth quarter," Chairman Philip Fletcher said in a statement.
For fiscal 1996 ended May 26, ConAgra reported earnings excluding non-recurring charges of $2.34 a share, up from $2.06 in fiscal 1995.

ConAgra today reported earnings for the first quarter ended August 25 of $0.42 a share, up from $0.36 a year ago. Net sales dropped to $6.40 billion from $6.44 billion due to business dispositions and lower beef selling prices.
ConAgra said its grocery/diversified products segment saw a 19 percent rise in operating profit and a nine percent increase in sales in the first quarter versus a year ago.
ConAgra said its two largest grocery products businesses, Hunt-Wesson and ConAgra Frozen Foods, each saw a double-digit rise in operating profit in the first quarter.

Golden Valley's microwave foods operating profit increased substantially. Lamb-Weston's potato products earnings were ahead of plan but moderately below last year's strong first-quarter results, it said.
ConAgra's refrigerated foods operating profit dropped eight percent, and sales declined four percent.
ConAgra said first quarter earnings were on plan and were consistent with expectations for significant profit growth in the second half and full year.
The sales decline was caused by beef and poultry business dispositions last year as well as lower selling prices in the U.S. beef industry, it said.

In the U.S. beef business, it said, first quarter operating profit declined moderately compared to strong earnings last year. The pork products business increased operating profit significantly, it added.
High costs for grain-based feed ingredients caused a drop in poultry products operating profits. Processed meats earnings were down, while cheese products earnings rose substantially, ConAgra said.
